questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-\frac{9}{2} \\  & y=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=\frac{1}{2}$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(\frac{1}{2})=-\frac{9}{2}\,⇒\,x=-\frac{9}{2}+\frac{3}{2}=-3.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-3$ and $y=\frac{1}{2}.$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y=8 \\  & y=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-11$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-11)=8\,⇒\,x=8+11=19.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=19$ and $y=-11.$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+7y=-2 \\  & y=-1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+7(-1)=-2\,⇒\,x=-2+7=5.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=5$ and $y=-1.$

questions.problem:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 16 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{16}\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{13}{16}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y=6 \\  & 4x-7y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=3 \\  & y=-2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-2)=3\,⇒\,x=-1.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-1$ and $y=-2.$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+8y=22 \\  & 7x-5y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 22 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 22 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 0 & -\frac{71}{3} & -\frac{142}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{3}{71}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

{\begin{aligned} & 3x-2y=4 \\  & 2x-y=2.\end{aligned}

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+\frac{1}{3}y=11 \\  & 3x+\frac{1}{5}y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 0 & -\frac{4}{5} & -24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{5}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 30\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+\frac{1}{3}y=11 \\  & y=30,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=30$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+\frac{1}{3}(30)=11\,⇒\,x=11-10=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1$ and $y=30.$
